roles.name: --accent-foreground
roles.purpose: text on an accent surface

roles.name: --destructive
roles.purpose: a destructive action — a delete or discard button, a destructive menu item

roles.name: --destructive-foreground
roles.purpose: text on a destructive fill

roles.name: --destructive-hover
roles.purpose: a destructive fill under the pointer

roles.name: --disabled
roles.purpose: the fill of a disabled control

roles.name: --disabled-border
roles.purpose: the border of a disabled control

roles.name: --disabled-foreground
roles.purpose: text and icons on a disabled control

roles.name: --feedback-danger
roles.purpose: an error message — a failed save, a field that will not take its value — as text

roles.name: --ghost-hover
roles.purpose: a borderless (ghost) control under the pointer

roles.name: --icon-alert-titled
roles.purpose: an alert's icon beside a title and its text — the same line weight, drawn larger

roles.name: --icon-body
roles.purpose: an icon in a line of body or button text

roles.name: --line-height-body
roles.purpose: prose, rows, labels and controls
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --muted-foreground
roles.purpose: secondary text — hints, metadata. L .50 is the lightest that clears WCAG AA (4.5:1) on every surface muted text sits on, muted and accent included

roles.name: --outline-border
roles.purpose: an outline button's border

roles.name: --outline-fill
roles.purpose: an outline button's fill

roles.name: --outline-hover
roles.purpose: an outline button under the pointer

roles.name: --primary
roles.purpose: the brand fill: the one primary action per view, the active nav item

roles.name: --primary-foreground
roles.purpose: text and icons on a primary fill

roles.name: --primary-hover
roles.purpose: a primary fill under the pointer

roles.name: --primary-ink
roles.purpose: the brand colour as TEXT or a glyph on a surface — a link, a record's mark. The fill above carries white text; in dark it is too deep to read as text itself, so this lifts it.

roles.name: --radius-control
roles.purpose: a thing that IS content: a button, a field, a nav item

roles.name: --ring
roles.purpose: the focus ring

roles.name: --secondary
roles.purpose: the secondary button fill — a neutral grey, distinct from accent

roles.name: --secondary-foreground
roles.purpose: text on a secondary fill

roles.name: --secondary-hover
roles.purpose: a secondary fill under the pointer

roles.name: --size-control
roles.purpose: a field, a default button; 44px under a touch pointer
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --size-control-affix
roles.purpose: a control attached to another element: a field's clear or open, a row's disclosure, a nav item's star, a dialog's close
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --size-control-embedded
roles.purpose: a control set inside another component's line: a table row, a banner, the pager, a filter panel
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --step-14
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: --weight-strong
roles.purpose: a row title, a field label, a button label, a badge, a dialog title
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.

roles.name: type-button-label
roles.purpose: the text on a button
roles.value: font-size: var(--step-14); font-weight: var(--weight-strong); line-height: var(--line-height-body)
roles.why: A back office is compact by definition: its gaps, its field and row sizes, its text sizes and weights and its page edge are part of what it is.
